name: E-Commerce / Retail Company
description: For e-commerce and retail companies where merchandising, supply chain, logistics, and fulfillment are core operational functions. Warehouse operations, inventory planning, and customer experience teams are central to the org structure. Designed for seasonal staffing surges (Black Friday/Cyber Monday) and strong integration between online and physical retail channels.

org_structure.overview: E-commerce orgs are operations-heavy with a strong focus on the physical flow of goods alongside the digital customer experience. The philosophy is 'bits and atoms' — technology and operations must be deeply integrated because a beautiful online store is useless if inventory is wrong or delivery fails. Supply chain, logistics, and fulfillment are first-class departments on par with Engineering and Product, not back-office functions. Seasonal demand patterns require flexible staffing models and surge capacity planning. The org typically divides into three major pillars: Commercial (merchandising, buying, marketplace), Operations (supply chain, fulfillment, customer service), and Technology (platform, data, product). At companies with physical stores, store operations adds a fourth pillar with district/regional management layers.

departments.name: Executive Leadership
departments.description: C-suite that balances commercial performance (revenue, margin) with operational excellence (delivery speed, inventory efficiency).

roles.title: Chief Executive Officer (CEO)
roles.description: Sets overall strategy, brand vision, and company culture. Ultimate accountability for revenue, margin, and customer experience.

roles.title: Chief Operating Officer (COO)
roles.description: Owns supply chain, fulfillment, logistics, customer service, and store operations. Critical during peak season execution.

roles.title: Chief Commercial Officer (CCO)
roles.description: Owns merchandising, buying, pricing, revenue growth, and marketplace (if applicable). Drives margin optimization.

roles.title: Chief Technology Officer (CTO)
roles.description: Owns e-commerce platform, mobile apps, data infrastructure, and technology strategy. Builds the digital storefront and backend systems.

departments.name: Merchandising & Buying
departments.description: Core commercial function that selects products, manages inventory assortment, negotiates with suppliers, and sets pricing and promotions.

roles.title: SVP / VP of Merchandising
roles.description: Sets merchandising strategy, assortment planning, and vendor strategy. Owns gross margin by category.

roles.title: Director of Buying
roles.description: Leads buying teams by category (e.g., apparel, electronics, home goods). Negotiates with vendors and manages open-to-buy budgets.

roles.title: Buyer / Merchandiser
roles.description: Selects products, negotiates terms, manages inventory allocation, and plans promotions for assigned categories.

roles.title: Pricing & Promotions Manager
roles.description: Develops pricing strategy, competitive price monitoring, promotion calendar, and markdown optimization.

roles.title: Private Label / Product Development Manager
roles.description: Develops private label products, manages supplier relationships for owned brands, and coordinates with design and sourcing.

departments.name: Supply Chain & Logistics
departments.description: End-to-end supply chain from supplier to customer doorstep. Includes inbound logistics, warehouse operations, inventory planning, and last-mile delivery.

roles.title: VP of Supply Chain
roles.description: Supply chain strategy, network design, carrier relationships, and end-to-end supply chain performance.

roles.title: Director of Warehouse Operations
roles.description: Manages fulfillment centers / warehouses. Responsible for pick/pack/ship accuracy, throughput, and labor management.

roles.title: Warehouse Manager
roles.description: Day-to-day management of shift operations in a fulfillment center. Manages team leads and associates.

roles.title: Inventory Planning Manager
roles.description: Demand forecasting, inventory allocation across fulfillment nodes, safety stock optimization, and inventory aging management.

roles.title: Logistics / Carrier Manager
roles.description: Manages carrier relationships (FedEx, UPS, USPS, regional carriers), shipping cost optimization, and last-mile performance.

roles.title: Supply Chain Analyst
roles.description: Analyzes supply chain KPIs, supports network modeling, tracks carrier performance, and builds reporting dashboards.

departments.name: E-Commerce & Product Technology
departments.description: Builds and maintains the digital commerce platform: website, mobile app, checkout, personalization, search, and recommendation systems.

roles.title: VP of E-Commerce Technology
roles.description: Technology strategy for the e-commerce platform. Owns architecture, platform reliability, and engineering delivery for customer-facing systems.

roles.title: Director of Product (E-Commerce)
roles.description: Product strategy for the e-commerce experience: browse, search, PDP, cart, checkout, and post-purchase.

roles.title: Product Manager (E-Commerce)
roles.description: Owns a specific area of the e-commerce experience (e.g., search, checkout, my account, mobile app).

roles.title: Engineering Manager (E-Commerce)
roles.description: Manages engineering squads for areas like storefront, checkout, personalization, or CMS.

roles.title: Frontend Engineer (Web / Mobile)
roles.description: Builds customer-facing UI. Deep expertise in performance (Core Web Vitals, page load) and conversion optimization.

roles.title: Backend Engineer (E-Commerce Platform)
roles.description: Builds APIs for product catalog, cart, pricing, inventory, and order management systems.

departments.name: Customer Experience & Service
departments.description: Post-purchase customer support, returns management, and VOC (voice of customer) programs. Critical during peak season when support volume surges.

roles.title: VP of Customer Experience
roles.description: Customer experience strategy, service design, support operations, and NPS / CSAT ownership.

roles.title: Director of Customer Support
roles.description: Manages support centers, staffing models, quality assurance, and knowledge base. Owns SLAs and resolution times.

roles.title: Customer Support Manager
roles.description: Manages shifts of support agents. Handles escalations and team performance.

roles.title: Returns & Refunds Operations Lead
roles.description: Owns returns process, refund processing, reverse logistics, and return fraud detection.

departments.name: Marketing (E-Commerce)
departments.description: Demand generation specific to e-commerce: paid social, paid search, email/SMS, affiliates, and CRM. Strong focus on ROAS and customer acquisition cost.

roles.title: VP / Director of E-Commerce Marketing
roles.description: Digital marketing strategy, channel mix, budget allocation, and ROAS targets.

roles.title: Performance Marketing Manager
roles.description: Paid search (Google Shopping, Bing), paid social (Meta, TikTok, Pinterest), and affiliate marketing.

roles.title: Email & SMS Marketing Manager
roles.description: Lifecycle email/SMS campaigns, abandoned cart recovery, post-purchase flows, and segmentation.

roles.title: CRM / Retention Marketing Manager
roles.description: Customer loyalty program, VIP tiers, personalized recommendations via email, and reactivation campaigns.

roles.title: Creative / Content Producer
roles.description: Creates ad creative, product photography, video content, and social media content for campaigns.

key_relationships: Merchandising and Supply Chain are tightly coupled — inventory buys must align with warehouse capacity and delivery timelines. Weekly cross-functional review of open-to-buy vs. fulfillment capacity.
E-Commerce Product and Technology work as integrated squads with shared OKRs around conversion rate, average order value, and page load speed.
Marketing coordinates closely with Merchandising on promotion calendar and inventory availability — no promotion is launched without confirmed stock levels.
Customer Experience feeds returns and complaint data back to Merchandising (product quality issues) and Supply Chain (delivery issues).
A peak season (BFCM) cross-functional task force forms 3 months in advance, including representatives from every department.
The CCO and COO hold a weekly joint operations review covering inventory turns, fulfillment accuracy, on-time delivery, and customer satisfaction.
Data Science supports all teams with demand forecasting, personalized recommendations, price optimization, and customer churn prediction.
Warehouse Operations and Customer Support share a real-time dashboard during peak season, so support knows about shipping delays before customers call.
